findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses pub status: String and independent bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum typestate. Any string value is valid for status (e.g. 'pending', 'garbage', 'sent' duplicated in both fields), and is_validated/is_sent can be in inconsistent combinations (is_validated=false, is_sent=true).
findings.failure_mode: A packet can exist in an invalid lifecycle state such as validated=false but sent=true, or status='pending' but is_sent=true, allowing downstream logic to process packets that should be rejected.
findings.fix:
Replace status: String with a sealed enum Status { Pending, Validated, Sent, Rejected }. Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a typestate enum (e.g. PacketState

) or a single status field that is the source of truth. Make all fields private behind impl methods.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates in-place via &str to_string allocation, returning the struct directly instead of using a Result or the typestate pattern. The function name implies an action but the type signature is a pure transform with hidden allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to mark_sent heap-allocates a new String for status even though the value is always the literal 'sent'. This is wasteful and the function provides no error channel for future constraints (e.g. rejecting mark_sent on non-validated packets).
findings.fix: Define an enum Status and a typestate PacketWorkflow<S>. Use mark_sent(&mut self) -> Result<(), PacketError> that enforces domain invariants (must be validated before sent) and sets status = Status::Sent without allocation.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are public (pub id, pub status, pub is_validated, pub is_sent, pub sent_at_epoch_ms). This allows callers to construct or mutate the struct in illegal states bypassing any constructor invariants.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set is_validated=false and is_sent=true simultaneously, or set status to an arbitrary string, breaking all domain invariants the core is supposed to enforce.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a fallible constructor PacketWorkflow::new(id: String, status: Status) -> Result<Self, Error> that initializes all derived fields consistently. Expose only the needed read accessors (e.g. .id(), .status(), .is_sent()).

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new heap String for a known literal. The struct owns String fields unnecessarily when all status values are domain-known literals.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded heap allocation per transition. In a high-throughput packet processing path this becomes a measurable performance bottleneck with no correctness benefit.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a Status enum. No allocation needed for status transitions.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate lifecycle flags. These are the exact pattern the skill reference prohibits: 'Replace bool lifecycle flags, status strings, and Option lifecycle fields with enums or typestates.'
findings.failure_mode: The boolean flag space has 4 combinations but only 2 may be valid (validated=false/sent=false = pending; validated=true/sent=true = sent). The other 2 combinations are illegal states that the compiler cannot catch.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single Status enum: Pending, Validated, Sent. Or use a typestate system where the compiler tracks the current lifecycle stage.

findings.problem: mark_sent is named as an action (imperative shell) but has a pure function signature (PacketWorkflow -> PacketWorkflow). It mutates state but has no error return, no side-effect channel, and no typestate tracking.
findings.failure_mode: The function signature misleads callers into thinking this is a pure, deterministic transform with no failure mode, but in reality status transitions should enforce ordering invariants and could fail (e.g. sending an unvalidated packet).
findings.fix: Either make it a pure transform on a properly typed enum (mark_sent(status: Status) -> Status with pattern-match guards) or make it an imperative action returning Result<(), PacketError> with a mutable receiver.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for the packet processing hot path
no allocation tracing (e.g. dhat, heaptrack) for Vec/String growth in packet lifecycle
no second-ring validation evidence (no property tests or fuzz targets)
no command-level evidence: no cargo test, cargo bench, or cargo clippy output present
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has no benchmarks, no tests, and no typestate enforcement. The core domain model is untyped (String status, bool flags), making illegal states representable by construction. Any downstream consumer of PacketWorkflow must re-implement the invariants the type system should enforce.
